question: Does a logged, rerunnable replication of Card's college-proximity paper (NBER Working Paper 4483, 1993; published 1995 in the Vanderkamp volume, University of Toronto Press, pp. 201-222) from his public NLS Young Men extract (nls.dat) reproduce the published OLS and instrumental-variables estimates of the return to a year of schooling, with proximity to a four-year college in 1966 (nearc4) as the instrument for completed education; and, in the one-endogenous-regressor counterparts of the basic specification (experience treated as exogenous, Table 3 Panel A columns 6 and 5), how much of the IV conclusion survives inference that is robust to a weak instrument and to a bounded violation of the exclusion restriction? Because Panel A treats experience (age - education - 6) as exogenous although education is not, which Card himself flagged, the basic three-endogenous-regressor specification (Panel B column 6) also gets weak-instrument-robust subvector Anderson-Rubin inference, and the Panel A results are stated as results about the Panel A coefficient. This is a replication: the estimates are published and were exactly reproduced by Kling (2001), and these data have been reanalysed many times since; the paper claims no new finding about the return to schooling. (The seed task and Card's codebook cite NBER WP 4832; the Scout verified that the proximity paper is WP 4483.)
hypotheses: H1 (computational reproduction; targets verified by the Scout from the WP 4483 table images, sources/notes.md sec. 1): N = 3,010 men with a non-missing lwage76, unweighted. Primary target, Card's basic specification (Table 3 Panel B: experience and its square endogenous, instrumented by age and age squared; basic controls plus the 14 family-background variables): 2SLS return 0.132 (s.e. 0.049) in column 6 [claims iv-return, iv-return-se], first-stage coefficient on nearc4 0.365 (0.105) in column 2 [first-stage], reduced form 0.048 (0.019) in column 4; OLS 0.073 (0.004) from Table 2 column 5 [ols-return]. Secondary targets (the full list of 22, with values, is in design.method and is authoritative): Table 3 Panel A column 6 (experience exogenous, family background included): 2SLS 0.140 (0.055), first stage 0.322 (0.083), reduced form 0.045 (0.018), OLS Table 2 column 5; Panel A column 5 (no family background): 2SLS 0.132 (0.055), first stage 0.320 (0.088), reduced form (column 3), OLS 0.075 (0.003) from Table 2 column 2; Panel B columns 1, 3 and 5 (the no-family-background counterparts of columns 2, 4 and 6), and the homoskedastic Anderson-Rubin 95% set [0.025, 0.285] that Cinelli and Hazlett (2025, Table 2) report for this column. Comparison uses conventional (homoskedastic) standard errors, because the published formula is not stated and the printed 0.055 matches a conventional figure; heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors are reported alongside. Each printed number is reproduced if the replicated value rounds to it at the printed precision (|replicated - published| < half a unit in the last printed digit); N must match exactly. Kling (2001) printed the OLS standard error as .003 where Card printed .004, so that one value may sit on a rounding boundary; the replicated value is reported to four decimals. A failure is reported and diagnosed (sample rule, variable construction, standard-error formula), not tuned away. A pass is a computational check, not new evidence about the return to schooling.

H2 (instrument strength; primary specification Panel A column 6, the one-endogenous-regressor specification that keeps Card's family-background controls; Panel A column 5 reported alongside for comparison with the published literature): the conventional first-stage F on nearc4 is compared with the Stock-Yogo 10% maximal-size critical value for one instrument and one endogenous regressor (16.38), and the Montiel Olea-Pflueger effective F (with one instrument, the heteroskedasticity-robust first-stage F) with its 5%-size, 10%-worst-case-bias critical value (23.11). Each reported as above or below its threshold. The published first-stage t statistics (0.322/0.083 = 3.9; 0.320/0.088 = 3.6) imply F of about 15 and 13, so 'below' is expected and the hypothesis is mainly a check on the robust version; the result changes no specification. Neither threshold applies to the three-endogenous Panel B specification, for which no weak-instrument test is reported; that limit is stated.

H3 (weak-instrument-robust inference). (a) Panel A column 6 primary, column 5 alongside: the heteroskedasticity-robust Anderson-Rubin 95% confidence set for the Panel A coefficient on schooling. With one instrument, excluding 0 is the same event as the robust reduced-form t test rejecting, and the paper says so. (b) Card's basic specification, Panel B column 6 (schooling, experience and experience squared endogenous; nearc4, age and age squared as instruments; just identified): a subvector Anderson-Rubin set for the return to schooling with the experience coefficients as nuisance parameters, reported three ways: the homoskedastic subvector AR with the Guggenberger-Kleibergen-Mavroeidis (2019) data-dependent critical values, the same statistic with the chi-square(1) critical values of Guggenberger et al. (2012), and, as the primary version because both of those assume homoskedasticity, the heteroskedasticity-robust projection set (minimum over the nuisance coefficients of the robust full-vector AR statistic, compared with the chi-square(3) 5% critical value 7.815), which is valid but conservative. Decision rules fixed now, applied to each primary set separately: for (b), 'the IV return to schooling is positive' survives iff the set is a bounded interval whose lower bound is above 0; for (a) the same rule decides the narrower statement 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling is positive'. A set that is unbounded, a union of half-lines, or includes 0 is reported with its shape and bounds, not read as evidence of no return. The Panel A results concern the Panel A coefficient, which assumes experience exogenous; the paper reports the A6 and B6 estimates and sets side by side so the reader can see how much that assumption matters. Expected from the published numbers before any run: Card's Panel B reduced-form t is about 0.048/0.019 = 2.5 (t^2 about 6.4), below the chi-square(3) value 7.815, so the conservative robust projection set for H3(b) will very likely include 0; the paper reports that a 'does not survive' there may reflect the projection's conservativeness rather than the data, and reports the homoskedastic GKM19 and GKMC sets beside it without letting them decide.

H4 (exclusion-restriction sensitivity, descriptive; primary Panel A column 6, column 5 alongside; a statement about the Panel A coefficient, which assumes experience exogenous): Conley, Hansen and Rossi (2012) union-of-confidence-intervals with a direct effect gamma of nearc4 on log wages in [0, delta], built from Anderson-Rubin tests (so it is robust to a weak instrument): report the smallest delta (in log-wage units, so 0.01 is one log point) at which the robust 95% set for the Panel A coefficient on schooling first includes 0, and delta as a share of the replicated reduced-form coefficient. With one instrument this breakdown point equals the lower bound of the 95% interval of the reduced form; from the published conventional numbers it is about 0.045 - 1.96 x 0.018 = 0.010 for column 6 and 0.007 for column 5 (the latter matches Cinelli and Hazlett's reduced-form bound), so the replication mainly checks the robust version, and the paper states this equivalence. The Wald-based union of intervals is reported only as a secondary, non-robust comparison. As a reference scale the paper quotes Card's Table 5 direct-effect estimates (0.015 and 0.013) with the caveat that they come from the experience-endogenous, interacted-instrument model, and the direct-effect bounds of Steiner, Houssineau and Steel (2025), whose controls differ from Card's. No threshold: a breakdown point for the reader to judge.

H5 (IV vs OLS, the only test of the difference; primary Panel A column 6, column 5 alongside): a heteroskedasticity-robust control-function (Durbin-Wu-Hausman) test of the null that the Panel A 2SLS and OLS coefficients on schooling are equal (the coefficient on the first-stage residual is zero), two-sided at 5%; the robust standard error of that coefficient is valid under this null. Minimum detectable difference at 80% power, computed now from the published conventional standard errors with no data run: 2.8 x sqrt(0.055^2 - 0.004^2) = 0.154 for column 6 and 2.8 x sqrt(0.055^2 - 0.003^2) = 0.154 for column 5; the published point differences are 0.067 and 0.057, so a non-rejection is expected. The MDEs are approximations from conventional standard errors, while the test is heteroskedasticity-robust; the result is therefore reported with (i) a 95% Wald interval for the IV-OLS difference whose standard error comes from the joint (stacked) influence functions of the two estimators with HC1 scaling, labelled as not robust to a weak instrument, and (ii) whether the replicated OLS estimate lies inside the H3(a) robust AR set (descriptive; the OLS standard error is small relative to the IV one). A non-rejection is read through these, not as evidence that the two coefficients are equal. Because the 2SLS coefficient is not guaranteed to be a positively weighted average of returns on these data (see the contribution), and even under monotonicity and rich covariates it would weight men whose schooling responds to proximity, a difference from OLS is reported descriptively, not as a measure of ability bias.
contribution: A logged, rerunnable replication of a canonical IV estimate of the return to schooling (already reproduced by Kling 2001 and others), with published and replicated numbers side by side and every difference explained, and a correction of the working-paper number (WP 4483, not 4832) that circulates with the data. Weak-instrument-robust inference and exclusion-restriction sensitivity on these data are already published for the specification without family background (Cinelli and Hazlett 2025: homoskedastic Anderson-Rubin set and partial-R2 sensitivity) and, with a direct-effect parameterisation, for a different control set (Steiner, Houssineau and Steel 2025). The paper adds the heteroskedasticity-robust versions on the one-endogenous-regressor specification that keeps Card's family-background controls (Panel A column 6, chosen by the crew because the weak-instrument tools need a single endogenous regressor): effective-F thresholds, the robust Anderson-Rubin set and the Conley-Hansen-Rossi breakdown point, and states that with one instrument the last two are restatements of the reduced form. In the Scout's limited search these were not reported on that column. The paper adds no new estimate of the return to schooling. It does not read the IV estimate as the average return for all men: under monotonicity and correctly specified (rich) covariates it would be a positively weighted average of returns for men whose schooling responds to proximity (Angrist and Imbens 1995 for the weighted-average reading in general; Kling 2001 for its conditions with covariates), but on these data both conditions are in doubt: Blandhol et al. (2025) reject rich covariates for Panel A column 5, and Tubbicke (2023), for a binary some-college treatment on 2,988 men (a different estimand from Card's years of schooling), finds 2SLS well above estimators that do not rely on rich covariates and reports, citing Sloczynski, that reordering the instrument to allow for defiers halves 2SLS (0.570 to 0.289). So on these data even that reading is not guaranteed.

design.summary: From the 3,010 men in Card's nls.dat with a non-missing 1976 log wage, unweighted, we re-estimate by OLS and 2SLS (Python 3.14.6, linearmodels 7.1, statsmodels 0.15.0) every column of Card's Table 3 and Table 2 columns 2 and 5, with Card's basic specification (Panel B column 6: schooling, experience and its square instrumented by nearc4, age and age squared, base and 14 family-background controls; seed claims iv-return, iv-return-se, first-stage, ols-return) as the primary target, and count a printed coefficient or conventional (n-k) standard error as reproduced only if the unrounded replicated value rounds to it (9 primary and 22 secondary targets). Weak-instrument-robust inference is fixed for both specifications: for Card's Panel B column 6 a subvector Anderson-Rubin set for the return with the experience coefficients as nuisance parameters (primary: projection of the HC1-robust full-vector AR statistic against chi-square(3) = 7.815, own numpy/scipy code; alongside, not deciding: the homoskedastic GKMC set and the GKM19 set with Table 3 critical values, with the ivmodels 0.10.0 eq. (2.12)-quantile version and our own code as checks), and for Panel A column 6 (column 5 alongside), whose coefficient also assumes experience exogenous, the conventional and effective first-stage F against 16.38 and 23.11 (H2), the HC1-robust AR set (H3a), the AR-based Conley-Hansen-Rossi breakdown point for the Panel A coefficient (H4) and a robust control-function test of the Panel A 2SLS coefficient against its OLS counterpart with a stacked-influence-function Wald interval of the difference (H5); a set supports a positive sign only if it is a bounded interval above 0, and only the H3(b) set can support 'the return to schooling is positive' (the H3(a) set decides only 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling is positive'). Report-only checks that could weaken the reading (age 14-19 in 1966; nearc4 on KWW at ages 14-15, on KWW overall and on school-record IQ with its missingness; standard errors clustered on region-by-SMSA-1966 cells), a synthetic-data test of every estimator before the gate, and a comparison with Card's SAS listing read1.lst made only after every claim is written complete the plan; none of them can change a specification, a standard-error formula or a claim.
design.estimand: Panel B column 6 (Card's basic specification): the coefficient beta on ed76 in a linear equation for lwage76 in which ed76, exp76 and exp762 are endogenous and nearc4, age76 and age762 are the excluded instruments. Panel A columns 6 and 5: the coefficient on ed76 when exp76 and exp762 are treated as exogenous controls (the 'Panel A coefficient'); it equals the Panel B beta only if experience is uncorrelated with the wage error, which cannot hold exactly when schooling is endogenous because exp76 = age76 - ed76 - 6 (Card WP 4483 p. 13), so H2, H3(a), H4 and H5 are statements about the Panel A coefficient, not about the return to schooling. Neither coefficient is read as the average return for all men: under monotonicity and a correctly specified (rich) covariate adjustment the 2SLS coefficient would be, conditional on the covariates, a positively weighted average of returns for men whose schooling responds to proximity (Angrist and Imbens 1995; Kling 2001), but both conditions are in doubt: Blandhol et al. (2025) reject rich covariates for Panel A column 5, and Tubbicke (2023), for a different estimand (a binary some-college treatment, n = 2,988), finds 2SLS well above estimators that do not rely on them and, citing Sloczynski, that allowing for defiers halves 2SLS; so even that reading is not guaranteed here (sources/notes.md sec. 5 item 9).
design.identifying_assumption: (i) Conditional on the controls, nearc4 is unrelated to the unobserved determinants of 1976 log wages and affects them only through schooling, and it shifts schooling; (ii) in Panel B, age76 and age762 are likewise excluded (age affects wages only through experience given the controls, so no separate age or cohort effect), whereas Panel A instead assumes exp76 and exp762 uncorrelated with the wage error, an assumption that cannot hold exactly if ed76 is endogenous. In the data, (i) would be contradicted by nearc4 predicting the 1966 KWW score of men aged 14-15 in 1966 or the school-record IQ score given the controls (r-balance), by the estimate depending on men old enough in 1966 to have moved for college (r-age1419), and by large movement between columns 5 and 6 when family background is added; how much the Panel A experience assumption matters is shown by the A6 and B6 estimates and H3 sets side by side (h1-a6, h1-b6, h2h3-weakiv, h3b-subvector). The age exclusion in (ii) is maintained, as in Card, and no run tests it. None of these checks can confirm the assumptions.
design.method: SOFTWARE (code/requirements.txt, frozen by the Econometrician with pip freeze from a fresh venv; the Replicator rebuilds it with --setup): Python 3.14.6, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.5, scipy 1.18.1, statsmodels 0.15.0, linearmodels 7.1, ivmodels 0.10.0 (with its dependencies glum 3.5.0, tabmat 4.3.1, numba 0.68.1, llvmlite 0.50.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1; the Designer installed ivmodels 0.10.0 with numpy 2.5.3 and scipy 1.18.1 on Python 3.14.6 in a scratch venv on 2026-11-21 and ran its subvector AR test and inversion; if the resolver needs a different pandas, the frozen version is recorded and reported, not chosen by results). The only randomness is the 20 random starting values of the H3(b) minimisation, drawn with numpy.random.default_rng(4483). VARIABLES (as read1.sas; analysis file data/derived/card_analysis.csv from prepare-data, re-checked in ivlib.py): exp76 = age76 - ed76 - 6; exp762 = exp76^2 (Card prints its coefficient /100, which only rescales it); age762 = age76^2; f1-f8 = indicators for famed = 1..8 (famed = 9 omitted). Column sets: BASE_A = intercept, black, reg76r (South 1976), smsa76r, smsa66r, reg662-reg669 (region 1966 = 1 omitted), exp76, exp762 = 15 columns; BASE_B = BASE_A without exp76 and exp762 = 13 columns; FB = daded, momed, nodaded, nomomed, f1-f8, momdad14, sinmom14 = 14 columns. nearc2, nearc4a, nearc4b, weight, step14 and south66 are not used; kww and iq only in r-balance. SPECIFICATIONS AND k (k = number of right-hand-side columns including the intercept; n - k enters every conventional and HC1 SE). Panel A (experience exogenous): A1 first stage ed76 ~ nearc4 + BASE_A (k 16, n-k 2994); A2 = A1 + FB (k 30, n-k 2980); A3 reduced form lwage76 ~ nearc4 + BASE_A (16); A4 = A3 + FB (30); A5 2SLS lwage76 ~ ed76 + BASE_A, ed76 instrumented by nearc4 (16); A6 = A5 + FB (30). Panel B (experience endogenous): B1 ed76 ~ nearc4 + age76 + age762 + BASE_B (16); B2 = B1 + FB (30); B3 lwage76 ~ nearc4 + age76 + age762 + BASE_B (16); B4 = B3 + FB (30); B5 2SLS lwage76 ~ ed76 + exp76 + exp762 + BASE_B with excluded instruments nearc4, age76, age762 (16); B6 = B5 + FB (30), the primary specification. OLS: Table 2 col 2 lwage76 ~ ed76 + BASE_A (16); Table 2 col 5 = col 2 + FB (30). ESTIMATORS AND STANDARD ERRORS. 2SLS: linearmodels.iv.IV2SLS(dependent, exog, endog, instruments).fit(cov_type=..., debiased=True); OLS: statsmodels OLS. 'Conventional' = homoskedastic, sigma^2 = sum(e^2)/(n-k) with e the structural residual (IV2SLS cov_type='unadjusted', debiased=True; statsmodels default), as SAS PROC REG/SYSLIN print it; the H1 comparison uses it. 'Robust' = HC1, White's sandwich times n/(n-k) (IV2SLS cov_type='robust', debiased=True; statsmodels cov_type='HC1'); every H2-H5 statistic uses it. Diagnostic only (read only if an H1 standard-error target fails): the conventional SE with sigma^2 = sum(e^2)/n. Normal critical value 1.959964 for robust statistics. H1 DECISION (verdict): a printed number with d decimals is reproduced iff |replicated - published| < 0.5 x 10^-d, using the unrounded replicated value; N must equal 3010; OLS SEs are also written to four decimals. Primary targets (9): B6 2SLS 0.132, SE 0.049; B2 0.365, SE 0.105; B4 0.048, SE 0.019; Table 2 col 5 OLS 0.073, SE 0.004; N 3010. Secondary targets (22, every other printed nearc4 or education coefficient of Table 3 and Table 2 cols 2 and 5, plus the Cinelli-Hazlett set): A6 0.140 (0.055); A2 0.322 (0.083); A4 0.045 (0.018); A5 0.132 (0.055); A1 0.320 (0.088); A3 0.042 (0.018); Table 2 col 2 0.075 (0.003); B5 0.122 (0.046); B1 0.382 (0.114); B3 0.047 (0.019); homoskedastic AR set for A5 [0.025, 0.285] with critical value t(0.975, 2994)^2 (the degrees of freedom Cinelli and Hazlett report; chi-square(1) version written as a diagnostic). verdict writes both counts and every miss; a miss is diagnosed (sample rule, variable construction, SE formula) and never tuned away. H2 (h2h3-weakiv; A6 primary, A5 alongside): F_conv = (pi_hat / se_conv)^2 and F_eff = (pi_hat / se_HC1)^2 of nearc4 in A2 (A1); flags F_conv > 16.38 and F_eff > 23.11. No H2 statistic for Panel B (stated limit); h3b-subvector writes kappa_1 (below) as a descriptive measure of how strongly age identifies the experience coefficients. H3(a) (h2h3-weakiv; A6 primary, A5 alongside): robust AR(b0) = (lambda_hat - b0 pi_hat)^2 / (V_ll - 2 b0 V_lp + b0^2 V_pp), lambda_hat and pi_hat the nearc4 coefficients of A4 and A2 (A3 and A1), V their joint HC1 covariance from the two regressions on the same regressor matrix (n/(n-k) (W'W)^-1 [sum w_i w_i' e_i u_i] (W'W)^-1 at the nearc4 entries). Set = {b0 : AR(b0) <= 3.841459}, solved from the quadratic; checked inside the run against a grid (b0 in [-1, 1], step 1e-4) on which AR(b0) is recomputed as the HC1 t^2 of nearc4 in an OLS of lwage76 - b0 ed76 on nearc4 + controls (disagreement beyond one grid step fails the run). H3(b) (h3b-subvector; Panel B col 6). Notation: Z = (nearc4, age76, age762), k_Z = 3; W = (exp76, exp762), m_W = 2, nuisance coefficients g; X = BASE_B + FB (27 columns); n - 30 = 2980. (1) PRIMARY, heteroskedasticity-robust projection (own numpy/scipy code in ivlib.py; no Python library implements it): HAR(b0, g) = t' V^-1 t, t = the 3 coefficients on Z in the OLS of lwage76 - b0 ed76 - W g on Z and X, V their HC1 covariance. Computed from one stacked regression of (lwage76, ed76, exp76, exp762) on (Z, X): t = pi_y - b0 pi_ed - [pi_exp, pi_exp2] g and V = A S A' with S the joint HC1 covariance of the four Z-coefficient blocks and A = (1, -b0, -g1, -g2) kron I_3 (asserted equal to the direct regression at 20 random (b0, g) to 1e-8 relative). Profile m(b0) = min over g in R^2 of HAR(b0, g), minimised by scipy.optimize.minimize(method='BFGS', options gtol 1e-10) from (a) the 2SLS estimate of g in lwage76 - b0 ed76 ~ W + X with instruments Z, (b) the LIML estimate of g in that model, (c) g of the full B6 2SLS fit, and (d) 20 draws from N(start (a), diag(25 x squared HC1 SEs of the B6 g)) with default_rng(4483); m(b0) is the smallest value reached. Set = {b0 : m(b0) <= 7.814728} (chi-square(3) 95%), valid under heteroskedasticity whatever the instrument strength, and conservative (Andrews, Stock and Sun 2019). SET COMPUTATION (the same procedure for every H3(b) set: robust projection, GKMC, GKM19 (3T) and (3Q)): acceptance is evaluated on an ordered point list made of the fine grid b0 in [-1, 1], step 5e-4, and an outer grid of 400 log-spaced points on each side from |b0| = 1 to |b0| = 1e5. Every pair of neighbouring points in that list with different acceptance contains a boundary, found by bisection between the last accepted and the first rejected point (wherever it lies, inside or outside [-1, 1]) to an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 for |b0| <= 1 and a relative tolerance of 1e-6 beyond. The set is reported as its maximal accepted pieces, each with both bounds; a side is called unbounded only if every outer-grid point beyond the last crossing on that side, up to |b0| = 1e5, is accepted (then the piece is reported as running to +-infinity, with the note 'accepted up to 1e5'); otherwise a distant accepted piece is reported as a separate, bounded piece. The bound claims (b6-ar-*-lo/hi) are the lower bound of the lowest piece and the upper bound of the highest piece, with the number of pieces as a metric; pieces narrower than the outer-grid spacing outside [-1, 1] can be missed, which the paper states. (2) GKMC (Guggenberger et al. 2012), homoskedastic: AR_n(b0) = kappa_p, the smallest root of |kappa Omega(b0) - (Y0, W)' P_Z (Y0, W)| = 0 with Y0 = lwage76 - b0 ed76, all variables residualised on X, Omega(b0) = (Y0, W)' M_Z (Y0, W) / 2980; reject iff kappa_p > 3.841459 (chi-square(k_Z - m_W = 1)). (3) GKM19 (Guggenberger, Kleibergen and Mavroeidis 2019), homoskedastic: same statistic; reject iff kappa_p exceeds the conditional critical value c_0.95(kappa_1(b0), 1), kappa_1(b0) the largest root (it varies with b0). The critical value is computed two ways in the run: (3T) GKM19's own test, eq. (2.13): linear interpolation in kappa_1 of their Appendix B Table 3 column for k - m_W = 1 at 5% (values rounded up to one decimal by the authors), constant GKM19_TABLE3_KM1_5PCT in ivlib.py copied from the complete column the Scout transcribes into sources/notes.md sec. 4b (task s-gkm19-table); between tabulated points c is linear in kappa_1 (eq. 2.13); below the first tabulated point it is linear from (kappa_1, c) = (0, 0), as eq. (2.13) defines kappa_1,0 = 0 and q_0 = 0; above kappa_1 = 1000 it follows GKM19 fn. 4, c = (1 - F(kappa_1 - 1000)) x 3.838 + F(kappa_1 - 1000) x 3.841, where fn. 4 leaves the distribution function F open and we fix F(x) = 1 - exp(-x/1000) for x >= 0 (exponential, mean 1000; our choice, stated in the paper; any such F moves c by at most 0.003), so c is continuous and non-decreasing everywhere, as the size proof assumes (GKM19 p. 518). Appendix B (p. 522) says the tabulated quantiles are rounded upwards to one decimal; (3Q) the exact 95% quantile of the approximate conditional distribution, GKM19 eq. (2.12), as ivmodels 0.10.0 computes it (more_powerful_subvector_anderson_rubin_critical_value_function). THE REPORTED GKM19 SET IS (3T), because GKM19 define the test and prove its size with the tabulated, interpolated values; (3Q) is reported beside it, labelled 'eq. (2.12) quantile, ivmodels', with a flag for whether the two sets give the same decision on 0. Both sets are inverted by own code with the SET COMPUTATION above, using our kappa_1 scaled by 2980; the ivmodels set from inverse_anderson_rubin_test(critical_values='gkm') must agree with our (3Q) set to 1e-4 in each bound (ivmodels' anderson_rubin_test scales kappa_1 by 2981 rather than 2980; its p-values are therefore compared to 1e-3 only). Metrics: kappa_1 at the B6 2SLS estimate, at each reported bound of every set and its minimum over the grid; c(3T) and c(3Q) at the same points. Neither GKMC nor GKM19 decides H3(b). Software for (2) and the check of (3Q): ivmodels 0.10.0, ivmodels.tests.anderson_rubin_test(Z, X=ed76, y=lwage76, beta, W=(exp76, exp762), C=X without intercept, fit_intercept=True, critical_values='chi2' or 'gkm') and inverse_anderson_rubin_test(..., alpha=0.05) for the sets; ivmodels' statistic times (k_Z - m_W) equals kappa_p, with dfd = 2980. Our own kappa_p, kappa_1 and the GKMC set (closed-form quadric) are computed alongside on the real data; a disagreement above 1e-6 relative in the statistic or 1e-4 in a set bound fails the run (ivmodels scales kappa_1 by n - k_Z - 26 = 2981 rather than 2980, so the GKM19 p-value is compared to 1e-3). Decision rules (plan.json H3), each applied to its primary set separately: for H3(b) (robust projection, Panel B col 6) 'the IV return to schooling is positive' survives iff the set is a bounded interval with lower bound above 0 (flag h3b_b6_return_positive); for H3(a) (robust AR, Panel A) the same rule decides only the narrower statement 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling is positive' (flags h3a_a6_pacoef_positive, h3a_a5_pacoef_positive), and no H3(a) output, flag, claim or macro is labelled as a statement about the return to schooling. Otherwise the shape and bounds are reported as 'not established'. H4 (h4-chr; A6 primary, A5 alongside): the smallest direct effect delta at which the robust 95% set for the Panel A coefficient on schooling first includes 0; for outcome lwage76 - gamma0 nearc4 the H3(a) set has lambda_hat replaced by lambda_hat - gamma0. Breakdown delta* = lambda_hat - 1.959964 se_HC1(lambda_hat) (0 if negative), share = delta*/lambda_hat; confirmed on a gamma0 grid over [0, 0.05] (extended to 0.10 if needed), step 1e-5. Union sets at delta in {0, 0.005, 0.010, 0.015, 0.020} on a gamma0 grid of step 1e-4, written to runs/h4-chr/chr_grid.csv. Secondary, non-robust: the Wald-based CHR union (beta_hat - gamma0/pi_hat +- 1.959964 x its HC1 2SLS SE) and its breakdown on the same grid. H5 (h5-cf; A6 primary, A5 alongside): null that the Panel A 2SLS and OLS coefficients on schooling are equal. Test: v_hat = residual of A2 (A1); OLS of lwage76 on ed76 + controls + v_hat with HC1; rejects iff |rho_hat / se_HC1(rho_hat)| > 1.959964 (valid under its null rho = 0). Interval (i): D = Panel A beta_2SLS - beta_OLS (A6 minus Table 2 col 5; A5 minus col 2). With R = (ed76, controls), Q = (nearc4, controls), u the 2SLS and e the OLS residuals and e1 selecting ed76: psi_IV,i = e1' (R'P_Q R)^-1 R'Q (Q'Q)^-1 q_i u_i and psi_OLS,i = e1' (R'R)^-1 r_i e_i; Var(D) = n/(n-k) sum_i (psi_IV,i - psi_OLS,i)^2 with k = 30 (A6) or 16 (A5); interval D +- 1.959964 sqrt(Var(D)), labelled 'Wald, not robust to a weak instrument'. Inside the run, sum psi^2 x n/(n-k) for each estimator alone must equal its HC1 variance from linearmodels or statsmodels to 1e-8 relative, and D = -rho_hat g (g = coefficient on ed76 in an OLS of v_hat on ed76 + controls) is asserted as an identity, not used for the interval. (ii) Flag: whether the OLS estimate lies inside the H3(a) robust AR set (descriptive). Conventional Hausman t = D / sqrt(se_conv_IV^2 - se_conv_OLS^2) written for comparison with Card fn 17. MDE fixed from published SEs (plan.json H5): 0.154 for both columns. OTHER IDENTITY CHECKS (failure = run fails): A5 and A6 2SLS beta = lambda_hat/pi_hat to 1e-10; AR(0) of H3(a) = squared robust reduced-form t to 1e-10; exp76 = age76 - ed76 - 6 on every row; N = 3010 and no regressor missing.
design.data: Source: https://davidcard.berkeley.edu/data_sets/proximity.zip (nls.dat, 3,613 men, NLS Young Men 1976 cross-section; codebook code_bk.txt; read1.sas), fetched by fetch-data and recorded in data/manifest.json; analysis file data/derived/card_analysis.csv from prepare-data. Unit: man. Sample for every run unless stated: the 3,010 rows with non-missing lwage76 (equal to Card's N; the $1-$30 trim is already in lwage76 and is not re-applied); unweighted. r-age1419: age76 in 24..29 (age 14-19 in 1966; published N = 2037; a different count is reported and no other age rule is tried). r-balance: KWW (1966 interview) for men with age76 in 24..25 (age 14-15 in 1966, before college) and, separately, for all 3,010; IQ (school records) where non-missing (2,061 of 3,010 per data/CODEBOOK.md); counts reported. Outcome lwage76; endogenous regressor ed76 (and exp76, exp762 in Panel B); instrument nearc4; controls as in design.method. read1.lst, the SAS listing in the zip (PROC MEANS, a PROC CORR that includes ed76 and lwage76, PROC FREQ of nearc4 by nearc2, and PROC REG output for the OLS models of Table 2 columns 2 and 5), is outcome output and is used once only: nobody extracts, opens or parses it (prepare-data did not) until the H1-H5 runs, the report-only checks and verdict are recorded and their result claims are written to claims.jsonl. Then the single report-only run check-sas-listing reads it from data/raw/proximity.zip in memory and compares N, the ed76 coefficient and its standard error of both PROC REG models with the OLS metrics of h1-a5 and h1-b6 at the listing's printed precision. A match confirms the data reading and variable construction to more digits than Card's tables and settles nothing about the 2SLS SE formula. A mismatch is reported and diagnosed; any code fix it prompts is a deviation entered in design.deviations before the fix, reviewed in a new code round, and rerun with --replace so the first records stay under runs/.superseded and the paper reports both. The listing never selects a specification, sample rule or SE formula.
analysis_plan: 0a. fetch-data (data-prep, data-ra, code/fetch_data.py; task dr-fetch; done).
0b. prepare-data (data-prep, data-ra, code/prepare_data.py; task dr-prepare; done): data/derived/card_analysis.csv, data/CODEBOOK.md; read1.lst not used.

0c. check-synthetic (data-prep, econometrician, code/test_ivlib.py importing code/ivlib.py; before the gate, synthetic data only, numpy default_rng(4483); heteroskedastic errors in every design): conventional and HC1 SEs equal hand-coded matrix formulas; one-instrument 2SLS = reduced form / first stage; the analytic H3(a) set equals grid inversion in all three shapes (strong, weak, irrelevant instrument); AR(0) = robust reduced-form t^2; the CHR breakdown equals the reduced-form lower bound and the gamma0 grid; the stacked influence-function variance of each estimator equals its HC1 variance and Var(D) equals a 2,000-draw pairs-bootstrap variance within Monte Carlo error (tolerance stated in the script before it runs); H3(b), in two synthetic designs that mimic Panel B (3 instruments, 2 nuisance regressors, a quadratic-in-age-like structure, n = 3,010, 27 exogenous controls) with heteroskedastic errors (structural and first-stage errors multiplied by sqrt(0.25 + z1^2 + 0.5 z2^2), correlated across equations): S, strong nuisance (concentration parameter for W in the hundreds); WN, weak nuisance (first-stage coefficients of the instruments on W scaled so that the population kappa_1 is about 5). In both: the stacked HAR equals the direct HC1 Wald regression at 20 random (b0, g) to 1e-8 relative; at 10 values of b0 the BFGS profile minimum is no larger than the minimum of a brute-force 401 x 401 grid over g (centred on the LIML g, half-width 10 HC1 SEs per coordinate) times (1 + 1e-6), and is reported next to it; the robust projection set contains the true b0 in at least 0.95 - 3 x sqrt(0.95 x 0.05 / 500) = 0.921 of 500 heteroskedastic replications per design (the homoskedastic GKMC coverage in the same replications is reported, not asserted); own kappa_p, kappa_1 and the GKMC quadric equal ivmodels 0.10.0 (statistic 1e-8 relative, bounds 1e-6). GKM19 critical values: the ivmodels eq. (2.12) quantile at every finite tabulated kappa_1 of GKM19_TABLE3_KM1_5PCT satisfies table - 0.1 - 1e-3 < quantile <= table + 1e-6 (the table is the quantile rounded up to one decimal); at kappa_1 = 1000 |quantile - 3.838| < 1e-3; the (3T) interpolation returns each tabulated value exactly at its kappa_1, equals (kappa_1 / kappa_first) x q_first below the first tabulated point (e.g. half of it at half its kappa_1, 0 at 0), equals 3.838 at 1000, 3.838 + 0.003 x (1 - exp(-1)) at 2000 and tends to 3.841 (within 1e-6 at 1e5), and is continuous and non-decreasing on a grid from 0 to 1e5 (no step larger than the table slope times the grid step). Set computation: on synthetic quadrics with known roots (a bounded interval whose upper bound lies in (1, 2), a union of two half-lines, a bounded set plus a distant piece in (4, 6), and the whole line) the procedure returns the right pieces and bounds to its tolerances and calls a side unbounded only in the half-line and whole-line cases. Seeds: default_rng(4483) spawned per design. No real outcome is read.

1. h1-b6 (analysis, econometrician, code/h1_b6.py + ivlib.py): PRIMARY. Panel B col 6 2SLS (conventional and HC1), B2 first stage, B4 reduced form, Table 2 col 5 OLS, N; also Panel B cols 1, 3, 5 (secondary targets). Seed claims iv-return, iv-return-se, first-stage, ols-return.
2. h1-a6 (analysis, econometrician, code/h1_a6.py + ivlib.py): Panel A col 6 2SLS, A2, A4 (conventional and HC1).
3. h1-a5 (analysis, econometrician, code/h1_a5.py + ivlib.py): Panel A col 5 2SLS, A1, A3, Table 2 col 2 OLS, homoskedastic AR set with t(0.975, 2994)^2.

4. h2h3-weakiv (analysis, econometrician, code/h2h3_weakiv.py + ivlib.py): H2 conventional and effective F with threshold flags; H3(a) robust AR set (shape, bounds, flag h3a_*_pacoef_positive for 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling is positive') and robust reduced-form t; A6 primary, A5 alongside.

5. h3b-subvector (analysis, econometrician, code/h3b_subvector.py + ivlib.py): H3(b) for Panel B col 6: robust projection set (primary; flag h3b_b6_return_positive); GKMC set; GKM19 set with Table 3 interpolated critical values (reported) and with the eq. (2.12) quantile (ivmodels 0.10.0; labelled) and whether they agree on 0; own-code agreement checks with ivmodels; kappa_1 and both critical values at the 2SLS estimate and at every reported bound; profile m(b0), kappa_p(b0), kappa_1(b0) on the grid written to runs/h3b-subvector/profile.csv.

6. h4-chr (analysis, econometrician, code/h4_chr.py + ivlib.py): H4 AR-based CHR breakdown for the Panel A coefficient on schooling, share, grid confirmation, union sets at fixed deltas; Wald union secondary; runs/h4-chr/chr_grid.csv. A6 primary, A5 alongside; about the Panel A coefficient.

7. h5-cf (analysis, econometrician, code/h5_cf.py + ivlib.py): H5 (Panel A 2SLS vs OLS coefficient on schooling) robust control-function t, p, reject flag; D with stacked influence-function SE and Wald interval; OLS-inside-AR flag; conventional Hausman t. A6 primary, A5 alongside.

8. r-age1419 (analysis, econometrician, code/r_age1419.py + ivlib.py; report only): Card Table 4 row 7, the basic specification (B6 2SLS and Table 2 col 5 OLS) on men aged 14-19 in 1966; compared with the published 0.094 (0.064), OLS 0.076 (0.006), N 2037. Threat: older men moved near a college. Fixed reading: reported next to the full-sample estimate with both CIs; no claim changes.

9. r-balance (analysis, econometrician, code/r_balance.py + ivlib.py; report only), HC1 throughout, coefficient in points and in sample-SD units, N: (a) kww on nearc4 for age76 in 24..25 with BASE_B + FB + an indicator for age76 = 25 (age762 dropped: two ages); (b) kww on nearc4 for all 3,010 with age76 + age762 + BASE_B + FB (age, not experience, because experience contains schooling); (c) iq on nearc4 with the controls of (b), where iq is non-missing; (d) share with non-missing iq among nearc4 = 1 and nearc4 = 0, their difference and its HC1 SE (univariate). Fixed reading: in (a) and (c) a 95% CI excluding 0 is reported as evidence of selection on ability or of better schools near colleges, both threats to exclusion, with (c) qualified by (d) because the IQ subsample may be selected on nearc4; (b) is descriptive only, because a positive coefficient is also what a valid instrument produces through schooling completed by 1966. Nothing here changes a specification or claim.

10. r-cluster (analysis, econometrician, code/r_cluster.py + ivlib.py; report only): for A6 and A5, first stage and reduced form with CR1 SEs clustered on region-1966 (reg661-reg669) x smsa66r cells, G, the smallest cell size and the number of cells under 30 men, ratio to HC1, and the clustered reduced-form t against t(0.975, G-1). Fixed reading, both directions: a clustered t below its critical value means the paper says H3 and H4 depend on treating men as independent; a clustered t above it is not reported as robustness to county-level dependence, because CR1 with so few, unequal cells can itself over-reject.

11. verdict (analysis, econometrician, code/verdict.py; inputs the metrics of runs 1-10): H1 per-target flags, primary (of 9) and secondary (of 22) counts and the list of misses; H2 flags; H3(a) Panel-A-coefficient flags (h3a_a6_pacoef_positive, h3a_a5_pacoef_positive) and the H3(b) return flag (h3b_b6_return_positive); H5 reject flags; H4 breakdown next to the values predicted from published numbers (0.010 A6, 0.007 A5).

12. fig-chr (analysis, figures-ra, code/fig_chr.py; input runs/h4-chr/chr_grid.csv and runs/h3b-subvector/profile.csv): panel 1, robust AR-based union bounds against delta for A6 and A5 with delta* marked, Wald union dashed; panel 2, the H3(b) profile m(b0) with the 7.815 line and the GKMC/GKM19 sets marked; paper/figures/chr.pdf. No new statistic.

13. check-sas-listing (analysis, econometrician, code/check_sas_listing.py; input data/raw/proximity.zip and the metrics of h1-a5 and h1-b6): only after task e-claims is done; report only, see design.data.

Compute: H1-H5 are a few dozen linear regressions on 3,010 rows; h3b-subvector runs about 4,000 grid points x 23 BFGS starts on closed-form 3 x 3 quadratic forms (minutes at most); the whole plan fits the seed's 15-minute laptop budget, and the Econometrician reports the measured wall time.

h1-b6 also: iv-return-se-robust, first-stage-se, reduced-form, reduced-form-se, ols-return-se (four decimals in the paper), n-sample, iv-return-pct = 100 x (exp(beta_iv) - 1); b5-iv, b5-iv-se, b1-fs, b1-fs-se, b3-rf, b3-rf-se.
h1-a6: a6-iv, a6-iv-se, a6-iv-se-robust, a6-fs, a6-fs-se, a6-rf, a6-rf-se.
h1-a5: a5-iv, a5-iv-se, a5-iv-se-robust, a5-fs, a5-fs-se, a5-rf, a5-rf-se, a5-ols, a5-ols-se, a5-ar-hom-lo, a5-ar-hom-hi.
h2h3-weakiv: a6-f-conv, a6-f-eff, a5-f-conv, a5-f-eff (H2); a6-ar-lo, a6-ar-hi, a5-ar-lo, a5-ar-hi, a6-rf-t-robust, a5-rf-t-robust (H3a; an unbounded side is stated in the claim text with no value).

h4-chr: a6-pacoef-chr-breakdown, a6-pacoef-chr-share, a5-pacoef-chr-breakdown, a5-pacoef-chr-share; a6-pacoef-chr-wald-breakdown, a5-pacoef-chr-wald-breakdown (secondary). Claim texts say 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling', never 'the return'.

verdict: h1-primary-reproduced (of 9), h1-secondary-reproduced (of 22), h2-a6-sy-above, h2-a6-mop-above, h3a-a6-pacoef-positive and h3a-a5-pacoef-positive (text: 'the Panel A coefficient on schooling is positive', never 'the return'), h3b-b6-return-positive (the only flag about the return to schooling), h5-a6-pacoef-equality-rejected, and the a5 counterparts of the H2 and H5 flags.

Report-only: young-iv, young-iv-se, young-ols, young-n (r-age1419); bal-kww-young, bal-kww-young-se, bal-kww-young-n, bal-kww-all, bal-kww-all-se, bal-iq, bal-iq-se, bal-iq-n, iq-obs-diff, iq-obs-diff-se (r-balance); a6-rf-se-cl, a6-rf-t-cl, a5-rf-se-cl, a5-rf-t-cl, n-clusters, min-cluster-size (r-cluster); sas-ols-match (check-sas-listing, written after all other claims).
Published numbers are citation claims already in claims.jsonl (c-card-*, c-ch-ar, c-kling-replication); every result number in the paper comes through paper/numbers.tex macros.
deviations: D1 (track rule 'cluster standard errors at the level treatment varies'): nearc4 is assigned by 1966 county of residence, and nls.dat has no county or primary-sampling-unit identifier, so no H1-H5 statistic can be clustered at that level. H1 follows Card's (unclustered) SEs; H2-H5 use HC1, which assumes men are independent. r-cluster is a one-directional warning only; the paper states that every SE, AR set and the CHR breakdown may be too narrow.

D2: Card's basic three-endogenous-regressor specification (Panel B col 6) gets weak-instrument-robust subvector AR sets (H3b) but no instrument-strength test (H2), no exclusion-sensitivity breakdown (H4) and no IV-OLS test (H5); those are computed on Panel A, whose coefficient assumes experience exogenous, and the paper never calls Panel A col 6 Card's preferred specification.

D3 (recorded before any analysis run, answering code-r1 F2): two checks in h3b-subvector are implemented differently from design.method's wording. (a) The pointwise agreement with ivmodels 0.10.0 fails the run only for |b0| <= 1; for |b0| > 1 the difference is written as a metric, because exp76 + ed76 = age76 - 6 lies in the instrument span, kappa_1 grows with b0^2 and ivmodels' own root-finding loses precision at |b0| >= 1e3 (runs/NOTES.md items 2 and 10); set-level agreement (1e-4) is unchanged. (b) The 20 'random' (b0, g) HAR check points use 20 equally spaced b0 in [-0.5, 0.8] with the 20 rng(4483) g draws, so that the only randomness remains the starting points. Neither changes any estimate, set or decision rule.

D4 (post hoc, decided by the PI after the H1 runs, before the results review): one added report-only diagnostic run, diag-panelb, tests the hypothesis that Card's Panel B first-stage and reduced-form columns (B1-B4) were estimated with exp76 and exp762 kept in the equation as endogenous regressors instrumented by age76 and age762 (so that the printed reduced form divided by the printed first stage equals the printed 2SLS, as it does in Card's table and does not under the planned regressions). It cannot change any H1 target, verdict count or claim of the approved plan; its results are reported as a diagnosis of the B1-B4 misses, labelled post hoc.

D5 (rule fixed before the check-sas-listing run, answering code-r3 F6): if check-sas-listing exits non-zero, the failed run stays in the ledger; the Econometrician may then inspect only the line layout of read1.lst (every claim is already frozen); any fix is recorded here as a deviation and reviewed in code-r4 before a --replace run; if the reviewed fix still fails, the paper reports the check as not completed, and --unreviewed is not used. Per code-r3 F7 the sas-ols-match claim speaks only of Table 2 columns 2 and 5 (OLS) and N, all six comparisons are reported with their differences, and no tolerance is relaxed after the run.

D6 (answering results-r2 F9): analysis_plan step 8 asked for the r-age1419 and full-sample estimates with two confidence intervals side by side. The full sample is reported as beta (SE) through the iv-return and iv-return-se macros, with the H3(b) set as its interval, because h1-b6 writes no Wald interval metric; the age 14-19 subsample keeps its interval (young-iv-lo, young-iv-hi). No run was added.

D7 (added at the paper stage, decided by the PI): one descriptive analysis run, describe-sample, recomputes from data/derived/card_analysis.csv the Card Table 1 column 3 items for the 3,010-man sample (shares and means only; no statistic relating nearc4 to schooling or wages) and asserts equality with the values recorded by the prepare-data run, so that the data section can report them as macros (result claims must come from analysis runs). It changes no estimate, decision or count.

D8 (paper stage, with the human's consent in chat): the two axis labels of code/fig_chr.py said 'log points' for values in log-wage units. The labels alone were corrected and fig-chr rerun with --unreviewed, because the four code-review rounds were used; no statistic, check or input changed.
threats: T1 Sample or variable construction differs from Card's (sample rule, exp76, f1-f8, omitted region, South coded by reg76r): h1-b6, h1-a6, h1-a5 against 31 printed targets (verdict), prepare-data's checks against the codebook and Card's Table 1, the identity checks inside the runs, check-synthetic, and check-sas-listing after the claims are fixed.

T2 Card's SE formula is not stated, so an SE miss may be a formula difference: conventional (n-k) is fixed for H1 (h1-* runs), HC1 is reported beside it, and the n-denominator SE is a diagnostic read only if an SE target fails; the OLS SE (Card .004, Kling .003) may sit on a rounding boundary and is reported to four decimals (h1-b6, h1-a5).

T3 Data-file vintage: the 2002 public file may differ from the file behind the 1993 tables: h1-* and verdict report every miss with its size; check-sas-listing tests the code against Card's own program on this file, separating a code error from a vintage difference for the OLS models.

T4 Weak instrument (published implied F about 15 and 13 in Panel A, 12 in Panel B): h2h3-weakiv (H2 thresholds, H3a robust AR set) and h3b-subvector (H3b subvector sets); the paper reads the AR sets, not the 2SLS t, as the inference.

T5 Experience treated as exogenous in Panel A although exp76 = age76 - ed76 - 6 is correlated with the wage error whenever ed76 is (Card WP 4483 p. 13; design-r1 F1); the reduced form behind H3(a) and H4 also conditions on exp76: H2, H3(a), H4 and H5 are stated as results about the Panel A coefficient, and h1-a6 vs h1-b6 (published 0.140 vs 0.132 IV, 0.045 vs 0.048 reduced form) together with h2h3-weakiv vs h3b-subvector (H3a vs H3b sets) show how much the assumption moves the estimate and its robust set.
T6 Age is not excludable in Panel B (an age or cohort effect on wages beyond experience): maintained as in Card; h3b-subvector and h1-b6 rest on it, no run tests it, and the paper says so next to T5.

T7 Exclusion or independence of nearc4 fails (families who value schooling live near colleges, better local schools, local wage premia): h4-chr (direct effect that overturns the sign of the Panel A coefficient), r-balance (KWW at ages 14-15, IQ with its missingness), and the A5 vs A6 comparison (h1-a5, h1-a6).
T8 Proximity in 1966 reflects moves made for college by older men: r-age1419.
T9 Within-county correlation of the instrument and the errors (D1) makes HC1 inference too narrow: r-cluster (warning in one direction only); stated as a limitation of H2-H5 and H3(b).

T10 Heterogeneous returns and additive covariates: 2SLS is not the average return and may not be a positively weighted LATE (Blandhol et al. reject rich covariates for A5): no run in this design tests the weights; h5-cf reports the IV-OLS difference descriptively, the estimand wording above is the safeguard, and the Reviewer checks it at the paper gate.

T11 Coding or optimisation errors in the AR, projection, CHR and influence-function code: check-synthetic before the gate (heteroskedastic coverage of the projection set with strong and weak nuisance identification, brute-force minimisation in both, ivmodels agreement, GKM19 critical values against Table 3), the in-run assertions of h2h3-weakiv, h3b-subvector, h4-chr and h5-cf, and the code review before any analysis run.

T12 Tuning toward published numbers: specifications, SE formulas, decision rules and claim ids are fixed here; read1.lst is unopened until claims are written (check-sas-listing); any later change is a deviation run with --replace and reported.

question.summary: Replication of Card (WP 4483) IV return to schooling; H1 reproduction of Panel B col 6 and Panel A cols 6/5; H2-H5 weak-IV-robust and exclusion sensitivity on Panel A col 6 (col 5 alongside). Reviewer question-r2: pass, F7-F8 minor answered.

design.summary: Design fixed: H1 reproduction (9 primary + 22 secondary targets, conventional n-k SEs); H2-H5 on Panel A col 6 (col 5 alongside) labelled as Panel A coefficients; H3(b) subvector AR on Card's basic Panel B col 6 (robust chi2(3) projection decides; GKM19/GKMC homoskedastic alongside); synthetic-data checks before any analysis; read1.lst read once after claims. Reviews: literature-r2 pass, design-r3 pass, all findings answered.

results.summary: H1 primary 5/9, secondary 19/22 (all 7 misses in Panel B cols 1-4, reproduced 8/8 by the post hoc D4 diagnostic); B6 2SLS 0.132 (0.049) reproduced; H3(b) robust projection [-0.007, 0.498] includes 0: positive return not established (homoskedastic GKM19/GKMC exclude 0, not deciding); Panel A: AR sets above 0, F below thresholds, CHR breakdown 0.011, IV=OLS not rejected; SAS listing 6/6. results-r2 pass.

submission.summary: Paper (19 pp) after paper-r1 (revise) and paper-r2 (pass; F13-F15 minor answered); clean rerun passed 18/18 runs, 911 metrics, fresh venv from requirements.txt; final PDF differs from the reviewed one only in process macros (rerun status, review counts).
